messages:
maria.leung: Heads up — spotted something weird in staging backups. The DB snapshot uploaded last night appears to be SSE-S3 only (no CMEK header). tagging eng-sre and security.
jonathan_kim: Which job + object path?
maria.leung: s3://redwood-backups/staging/db/2025-11-04-02-03.sql.gz (from backup-job v2)
jonathan_kim: Ran a head-object, got: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256
# no x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id
```
looks like it landed without SSE-KMS. :eyes:
kevin_security: Any recent RBAC changes for backup-uploader/backup-svc? Missing kms:GenerateDataKey would cause SDK to fall back to SSE-S3.
ops_sam: I rolled an infra cleanup last night that removed some broad kms perms from the backup service account. I thought we scoped them down but maybe I removed the specific GenerateDataKey action by mistake.
tina_platform: We also started using ephemeral worker instances for the staging cluster last week; their instance profile might not have the new grant.
kevin_security: Can we check CloudTrail for PutObject events around 2025-11-04T02:03Z to confirm the principal and the requestParameters? Quick query snippet: 
```
eventName = "PutObject" AND requestParameters.bucketName = "redwood-backups" AND eventTime >= "2025-11-04T02:00:00Z"
```
sec-oncall-bot: :rotating_light: encops-checker detected object without KMS header: s3://redwood-backups/staging/db/2025-11-04-02-03.sql.gz — created alert ENC-2026-112 (severity: medium).
jonathan_kim: Mitigation plan: pause staging backup job, copy object to same key with SSE-KMS using our backup CMK, validate integrity, then resume. Example command: 
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-backups/staging/db/2025-11-04-02-03.sql.gz \
  s3://redwood-backups/staging/db/2025-11-04-02-03.sql.gz.copy \
  --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/backup-cmk
```
maria.leung: Need to confirm prod unaffected before we escalate to compliance.
ops_sam: Quick check of a recent prod snapshot shows x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id present (arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/prod-backup-cmk). Prod seems fine.
kevin_security: Root cause looks like the infra PR that pruned the backup-svc policy (PR #8842) removed kms:GenerateDataKey for the staging role. Behavior: SDK attempted KMS but failed and S3 accepted the Put as SSE-S3. Action items below.
maria.leung: Action items: 1) kevin: open rollback / policy patch to restore minimal kms:GenerateDataKey for backup-svc. 2) ops_sam: re-encrypt affected staging objects and record checksums. 3) tina: add CloudTrail alert for PutObject missing x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id. 4) me: open compliance ticket with evidence.
kevin_security: I'll draft a scoped policy change and add a targeted KMS key policy grant (kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:Decrypt for re-encrypt job). Also will add a unit test in the deployment pipeline to validate object metadata after uploads.
ops_sam: Starting re-encrypt job now. Using copy-with-kms approach and will keep originals until checksum verified. Posting job logs here when finished.
sec-oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-0456 created (P2) — keep discussion here.
maria.leung: Please also add a short runbook step to encops playbook for detecting missing CMEK on new uploads and an automated alert rule based on head-object sampling.
jonathan_kim: Quick suggestion for longer-term: implement ephemeral KMS grants pattern — backup job requests temporary Grant on key, uses it, then deletes the Grant. Minimizes long-lived IAM perms.
kevin_security: Agreed. I'll add that to roadmap and include design notes in the PR.
ops_sam: Re-encrypt finished for the single affected file; checksum matches after copy. Will run a small restore test to validate.
maria.leung: Thanks all. I'll file the compliance evidence ticket and schedule a 15-min postmortem tomorrow to capture process fix and prevent recurrence. :lock:
